display.purpose: Page title and every large money figure on a summary card. One per region.

headline.purpose: Section headings inside the page, such as History.

body.purpose: Default text: table cells, descriptions, form labels, buttons, empty-state copy.

label.purpose: Category chips and other small metadata. Sentence case only.

numeral.purpose: Money figures. Always tabular so columns align on the decimal.

shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Cards and the table container at rest. Applied on top of the hairline ring, never instead of it.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Dialogs and select menus — anything floating above the page.

shadows.name: hairline-ring
shadows.purpose: The universal surface separator. Every elevated surface carries it first.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Keyboard focus on any interactive control, paired with a border shift to the ring color.

motion.name: overlay-enter
motion.purpose: Dialog and select menu enter/exit: fade plus 95% zoom, with a 2px slide from the trigger side on menus.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Default easing for hover, focus, and color state changes on controls.

motion.name: press-nudge
motion.purpose: Tactile press response on every non-popup button.

narrative.overview:
A bank window that fits in a hand. The product is used standing up, one-handed, seconds after money moves — so every surface has to earn its place on a small screen, and the interface behaves like a teller who already knows why you walked up: it shows the balance, takes the entry, and gets out of the way.

The register is quiet and monetary. A single desaturated green (Vault Green) carries brand and action; money itself speaks in a separate two-tone language of emerald for income and red for outcome, and nothing else in the system is allowed to borrow those two colors. Type is a soft humanist sans (Nunito Sans) run at small sizes with tight tracking, with tabular figures wherever a number can be compared to another number. Surfaces are near-white paper with hairline rings, gently lifted so a card reads as a physical slip rather than a painted rectangle.

Density is compact by intent — 32px controls, 16px card padding, 16px gaps — because the design starts at a phone and grows outward, never the reverse. What it rejects: crypto-fintech neon (glassmorphism, gradient glow, purple-to-cyan), corporate bank blue (navy chrome, enterprise widget density), and playful cartoon budgeting (mascots, confetti, pastel gamification).
keyCharacteristics: Mobile-first density: 32px control height, 16px rhythm, thumb-reachable primary action
One brand green, held apart from the money colors
Emerald/red as a strict semantic pair, never decoration
Tabular numerals on every figure, right-aligned in tables
Near-white paper, hairline rings, gentle ambient lift
Rounded but not soft: 7.2px base radius, pill only for category chips

rules.name: The Money Duotone Rule
rules.body: Emerald and red mean income and outcome. Nothing decorative may use them — no emerald success toasts, no red badges for non-financial state. If a color on screen is emerald or red, a user is entitled to read it as money direction.

rules.name: The Single Accent Rule
rules.body: Vault Green is the only brand color. Never introduce a second accent hue for a new feature; reach for neutral weight, position, or the money duotone instead.

rules.name: The No-Tinted-Card Rule
rules.body: Card backgrounds equal the page background. Depth comes from the hairline ring and ambient lift. A card that tints itself is a card that has stopped being paper.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every rendered amount and date carries tabular-nums. Figures that sit in a column must align on the decimal, at any weight or size.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Nunito Sans carries display, body, and label. Hierarchy is made from weight, size, and tracking — never from a second display face.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: All UI copy is sentence case, including buttons and headers ("New transaction", "Total income"). No uppercase labels, no title case.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: The layout is one column that widens. Multi-column arrangements are permitted only inside a region (the summary grid), never as page structure.

rules.name: The Scroll-Don't-Squeeze Rule
rules.body: Tabular data scrolls sideways in its own container. Never shrink a money column to fit, never truncate an amount.

rules.name: The Ring-First Rule
rules.body: Every elevated surface gets the hairline ring first; shadow is added on top of it, never in place of it. In dark mode the ring becomes oklch(1 0 0 / 10%) and the shadow all but disappears — depth there is carried by the lighter card fill.

rules.name: The Two-Step Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two elevations: resting and overlay. Nothing sits between them, and nothing stacks above an overlay.

rules.name: The Circle-Means-Icon Rule
rules.body: Full-round shapes are reserved for category chips and icon wells. A rectangular element never becomes a pill to attract attention.

dos: Do put every amount and date in tabular figures, and right-align amounts in any column.
Do keep money in the duotone: Income Emerald for income, Outcome Red for outcome, Ink for a neutral total.
Do size controls at 32px with the 4/8/16/24/32/40 spacing ladder — the phone is the design target.
Do separate surfaces with the 1px foreground/10 ring first, then the Resting shadow.
Do write UI copy in sentence case, and label a busy button with its action in progress ("Saving…").
Do give every icon-only control an aria-label and every decorative icon aria-hidden="true".
Do let tabular regions scroll horizontally inside their rounded container.
donts: Don't introduce a second brand accent, gradient, or glow — Vault Green is the only brand color.
Don't use emerald or red for anything that is not money direction.
Don't tint a card background away from the page background to suggest depth.
Don't uppercase or letter-space labels, or add a second typeface.
Don't truncate, abbreviate, or round an amount to make a column fit.
Don't stack a third elevation level, or float anything above a dialog.
Don't reach for navy chrome, enterprise widget density, mascots, confetti, or pastel gamification.
